summary: This week's technology developments highlight major advancements in AI developer tools, browser engine innovation, cloud ecosystem integration, and privacy-focused web services.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
items.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude Ship, a developer tool that enables AI agents to handle routine code approvals, reviews, and fixes. This new capability aims to eliminate software development bottlenecks as AI-generated code volume continues to grow.

items.title: Ladybird, the first new browser engine in years, is now available to test
items.summary: The independent web browser Ladybird has released its alpha version for macOS and Linux after four years of development. Featuring a completely new engine built from scratch, it provides a rare alternative to dominant browser engines like Blink, Gecko, and WebKit.

items.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
items.summary: Google is updating its AI Mode in Search by integrating data from Google Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini application. This integration leverages existing ecosystem data to deliver significantly more personalized user responses.

items.title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
items.summary: Amazon has acquired Decart's artificial intelligence optimization technology and research team in a reported $7.5 billion deal. The acquisition strengthens Amazon's hardware capabilities as it prepares to sell its custom Trainium chips.

items.title: Google alternative Kagi launches an email service
items.summary: Search provider Kagi has announced the public beta launch of Kagi Mail, an ad-free email service designed to compete with Gmail. Built on open standards, the new platform provides users with custom domain support and 50GB of storage.
